images.alt: Information graphic with a light grey background and a dark blue bell icon at the top. Large heading reads ‘ANNOUNCEMENT’. Below, text states: ‘From 1 April 2026, 8 anti‑seizure medicines will be subject to a cautionary advisory label, warning of the risks associated with taking them during pregnancy.’ At the bottom are the Te Kāwanatanga o Aotearoa New Zealand Government logo and the Ministry of Health Manatū Hauora logo

Information graphic titled ‘Example of the new cautionary advisory label’. At the top is a yellow warning label with an icon and text stating: ‘Talk to your prescriber if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or are breastfeeding’. Below, text explains that the label will be applied to the following anti‑seizure medicines: Carbamazepine, Ethosuximide, Oxcarbazepine, Phenobarbitone, Phenytoin, Primidone, Sodium valproate, and Topiramate. At the bottom are the Te Kāwanatanga o Aotearoa New Zealand Government and Ministry of Health Manatū Hauora logos.

post.text:
8 anti-seizure medicines in NZ now carry a new pregnancy cautionary advisory label — the first pharmacist added pregnancy warning of its kind. The label is designed to highlight the risks of taking certain anti-seizure medicines during pregnancy.
